official.application_cycle: 9th edition call, announced as no. 12/2026 on 13 March 2026; projects must start between 1 March and 1 October 2027
official.status_note: The call announced on 13 March 2026 closed on 29 May 2026 at 3:00 p.m. Polish time; the announcement states that results are planned for announcement by 31 January 2027, and the programme runs as an annual edition.
official.tuition_coverage_note: No tuition funding is published. The Announcement funds a monthly scholarship and lump sums for living, accommodation and travel, and states: "The Programme does not provide financial resources for institutions (indirect costs) or research costs (e.g. materials, reagents or participation in conferences)" and "Insurance and visa costs, if required, are borne by the Scholarship Holder".
benefits: Monthly scholarship of PLN 3,750 for a doctoral student or PLN 7,500 for a person with a PhD, for each month of the stay at the host institution
Lump sum for living and accommodation costs for each month of the stay: PLN 4,000 (Group I countries), PLN 6,000 (Group II), PLN 8,000 (Group III), PLN 12,000 (United States of America)
Lump sum for travel costs, the total amount for a round trip: PLN 1,000 to PLN 6,500 depending on the country of destination
The lump sum for living and accommodation costs may be increased by PLN 2,000 per month at the Scholarship Holder's request where the holder has a certificate of severe or moderate disability
A monthly allowance of PLN 2,000 is available for each month of the stay if the Scholarship Holder has an underage child or children
The funds are free of income tax pursuant to Art. 21(1) point 39a of the Act of 26 July 1991 on personal income tax
eligibility: A person who permanently resides in Poland and is a doctoral student studying at a doctoral school referred to in the Act of 20 July 2018 Law on Higher Education and Science

Or a scientist, which means a person with at least a doctoral degree or an equivalent degree obtained abroad, whose primary place of employment at the time of submitting the application is the entity referred to in Art. 7(1) points 1, 2 and 4-7 of the Act on Higher Education and Science (a "visiting" position does not constitute employment requirements)

At least 1 achievement in the case of a doctoral student, or 3 achievements in the case of persons with a doctoral degree, in the last 5 years (counted from the beginning of 2021), from the categories listed in the Announcement
The Programme is open to representatives of all fields of science; representatives of the arts may participate provided that the activities planned in the project are of a scientific nature

Excluded from participation are natural persons who are citizens of the Russian Federation, as well as institutions and other entities based on the territory of the Russian Federation in the role of a Host Centre

A person who has already submitted an application for another NAWA scholarship programme cannot apply until it is resolved with a final and binding negative decision, and a beneficiary of another NAWA programme cannot apply until the scholarship is settled; Bekker Scholarship Holders may reapply after a waiting period of two consecutive recruitment rounds following the submission of a final report
requirements: Each Applicant may submit only one application for funding in a given call, covering a visit to one host institution
The application must be completed in English; applications submitted in any other language will not be considered
Publications should be presented in Polish or English; publications in other languages are allowed only where that language is the primary language of the publication for a given discipline

Mobility may last not shorter than 3 months and not longer than 24 months, stated in the application as the number of full months, and should be implemented on a continuous basis, with a possible suspension of the Project for a total period not exceeding 3 months (no funding is provided for the suspension period)

The Scholarship Holder must possess at least basic health insurance for all participants of the trip, including the costs of treatment and transport to hospital; an EHIC card or another policy of that scope is recognised where the host centre is in the EU or EFTA

Timely reports are required: confirmation of the commencement of activities at the Host Centre within 1 month of the Project start, an interim report for Projects longer than 12 months, and a final report within 30 days from the end of the Project
documents: An invitation from the host institution issued during the call for applications period, confirming the will to accept the Applicant, prepared on the letterhead of the host institution in accordance with the template in the Appendix to the Announcement

Copies of the Applicant's required achievements: the full text of a publication, a confirmation of acceptance for publication, or for a monograph the title page, ISBN page, editorial page, table of contents and selected fragments totalling no more than 20 pages

For representatives of the field of art: a copy of the catalogue with an ISBN number confirming presentation of the work in a foreign institution or academic centre, a copy of an award in an international competition, or other formal confirmation of artistic achievement

For doctoral students: a document confirming the status of a doctoral student, and an opinion of the supervisor at the doctoral school about the candidate and the planned project/programme of the visit

For persons with a doctoral degree: a document confirming the doctoral degree with an officially certified translation into English or Polish if the original language is other than English or Polish, and a certificate from the human resources department confirming the period and form of employment, dated no earlier than the date of announcement of the recruitment and issued in Polish
Statement templates published by the programme for supplementary situations: a statement on travel by own car and a statement of family stay
selection_criteria: Preliminary assessment by the Assessment Team (15 points): the Applicant's scientific or academic career and scientific accomplishments, and the extent to which the Applicant's scientific output is recognised at their career stage

Reviewers, arithmetic mean of both scores (45 points): career and accomplishments 15; justification for choosing the host institution 10; scientific quality of the Project 10; potential impact of participation on the Applicant's further scientific career 10

Evaluation Team (40 points): justification for the host institution, including its international recognition and the scientific standing of the supervisor, 10; scientific quality of the Project 15; potential impact of participation 15

Applications are subject to formal and merit-based assessment in accordance with the Regulations of NAWA programmes for natural persons; applications that do not receive a recommendation from the Assessment Team are not referred for further assessment

An application which is awarded fewer than 60 points in total in the merit-based assessment is considered not to meet the quality requirements and receives a negative merit-based assessment (Regulations of NAWA programmes for natural persons)
coverage: The scholarship for each month of the Scholarship Holder's stay in the host institution
Lump sum for living and accommodation costs for each month of the stay in the country where the host institution is located, by country group
Lump sum for travel costs, which is the total amount for a round trip
Possible increase of the living and accommodation lump sum by PLN 2,000 per month with a certificate of severe or moderate disability
Possible PLN 2,000 monthly allowance where the Scholarship Holder has an underage child or children, due regardless of whether the children participate in the trip
Not covered: research costs such as materials, reagents or participation in conferences, financial resources for institutions (indirect costs), and insurance and visa costs
application_method: Submit the application only in electronic form via the Agency's IT system: https://programs.nawa.gov.pl
Complete the entire application in English
Attach to the application form all information required and the documents listed in the Announcement
If more than one application is submitted, the application submitted last according to the time of submission in the NAWA ICT system is subject to evaluation
official.application_route: Electronic application only, submitted through the NAWA ICT system at https://programs.nawa.gov.pl, prepared entirely in English, with all required attachments.
official.citizenship_residency: The Applicant must permanently reside in Poland; the Announcement does not require Polish citizenship, but excludes citizens of the Russian Federation from participation.
official.international_eligibility: Nationality is not a formal criterion: eligibility rests on permanent residence in Poland and on employment or doctoral-student status at a Polish entity, so foreign nationals permanently resident in Poland may apply; citizens of the Russian Federation are excluded.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Open to all fields and disciplines of science; representatives of the arts may participate provided the planned activities are of a scientific nature. There are no restrictions on the country of the Host Institution, except the Russian Federation.
official.research_requirement: Eligible activities are international mobility consisting of internships and conducting scientific research or development work, with teaching or lecturing possible as a supplement. The Applicant must demonstrate achievements in the categories listed in the Announcement and describe a Project in the application.
official.duration: Research fellowships of 3 to 24 months, stated in full months; the Project implementation period (contract period) covers the mobility period plus 3 months, and the Programme implementation period runs from 1 March 2027 to 31 December 2029.
official.description: The Bekker NAWA Programme supports the international mobility of PhD students, scientists and academic teachers from Polish scientific and academic units by financing stays at renowned foreign research and academic centres, so that they can complete part of their doctoral education or research work with outstanding scientists abroad and build long-term relationships with foreign teams. NAWA reports 996 beneficiaries across eight editions in 46 countries, with Cambridge, Oxford and MIT among the most frequently chosen hosts.
official.region: Europe (Poland); host centre in any country except the Russian Federation
official.program_type: Outgoing international research mobility fellowship (monthly stipend plus lump sums) for Poland-based PhD students, scientists and academic teachers
official.english_requirement: The application must be completed in English and applications submitted in any other language will not be considered; publications should be presented in Polish or English. No IELTS or TOEFL score requirement is published.

verification.notes: All amounts, deadlines, eligibility rules and document lists were taken from the official 9th edition call no. 12/2026 of 13 March 2026 (English announcement PDF and the Announcement, documents-for-download and information-for-applicants pages on nawa.gov.pl), cross-checked against the programme description page and the NAWA news announcement.

applicant_utility.summary: Bekker NAWA pays PLN 3,750 a month to doctoral students and PLN 7,500 a month to PhD holders, on top of a living lump sum of PLN 4,000-12,000 a month set by the host country's cost group and a one-off round-trip travel payment of PLN 1,000-6,500. A 12-month fellowship in the United States is therefore funded at roughly PLN 19,500 per month before any family or disability supplements, but tuition, research costs, insurance and visa fees stay with the scholar. The 9th edition closed on 29 May 2026, so the realistic target is the next annual round, which NAWA has launched each spring with a late-May deadline and results announced by the end of January. In practice the award follows a publication record in Scopus, Web of Science, ERIH+ or CORE/DBLP venues far more than the elegance of the research idea, and it needs a dated invitation letter from the host centre.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Polish-based doctoral students with one qualifying indexed publication and PhD holders employed at a Polish university or research institute with three such publications, who already have a named supervisor abroad willing to send a formal invitation.
application_readiness_checklist: Count your qualifying achievements now against the five listed categories and check that each falls within the last five years counted from the beginning of 2021; for PhD holders you need three, for doctoral students one
Secure a host supervisor early and ask them to issue the invitation on institutional letterhead using the exact model provided in the Appendix, dated after the call opens and before the deadline
Ask your HR department for the employment certificate well in advance: it must be dated no earlier than the day the call is announced and must be issued in Polish
Prepare full texts of every achievement you cite, and for a monograph trim the extract to no more than 20 pages exactly as specified
Request the supervisor opinion at your doctoral school early, since it must comment on both you and the planned visit programme
Set up or verify your account on the NAWA ICT system (programs.nawa.gov.pl) and draft the application in English, leaving time to upload attachments before 15:00 Polish time on deadline day
common_rejection_risks: An invitation letter that is undated, on plain paper, or not following the model template in the Appendix, which fails the formal check
Counting a publication that is only submitted, under review, or in a journal outside Scopus, SCI-Expanded, SSCI, A&HCI, ERIH+, CORE/DBLP, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus or IEEE Xplore
PhD holders who cannot document three qualifying achievements, or doctoral students who cannot document one, including achievements that fall just outside the five-year window
An HR certificate that predates the call announcement or is issued in a language other than Polish
Being blocked by another NAWA application still pending, or by a previous Bekker project not yet settled and not past the two-round waiting period
Losing points because the host justification, the standing of the host supervisor, or the realism of the 3-24 month plan is not argued convincingly
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and all research costs (materials, reagents, conference participation), indirect costs for the host institution, health and travel insurance, visa and residence-permit fees, and any relocation costs beyond the round-trip travel lump sum. Insurance and visa costs are explicitly borne by the Scholarship Holder, and no funding is provided for a project suspension of up to three months.
document_audit: Achievement evidence must match the claimed category exactly: full text for publications, acceptance confirmation where accepted but not yet published, and the specified pages of a monograph rather than the whole book
A doctoral degree obtained abroad needs an officially certified English or Polish translation, which takes time to obtain
The HR employment certificate carries a date rule (no earlier than the announcement date) and a language rule (Polish), so a template in another language will not pass
Attachments must be signed and scanned if in written form, or certified with a qualified electronic signature if submitted electronically; an unqualified scanned signature is rejected
Publications in languages other than English or Polish are only accepted where that language is the primary language of the discipline, so justify the choice in the application
The optional own-car travel statement and family stay statement must be filed through the programme's document page, not improvised
alerts: The 9th edition deadline has passed (29 May 2026, 15:00 Polish time); the next edition is expected on the same annual rhythm, roughly spring announcement and late-May deadline, with results by 31 January 2027
Funds cannot be paid before 15 March 2027, so do not plan the mobility start earlier than that even though projects may formally start from 1 March 2027
A stay shorter than 15 days in a month is funded at only half the monthly rate, so plan travel and start dates around full months
The project may be suspended for at most three months in total and that period is entirely unfunded
Mobility must be continuous and time outside the host institution is capped at 10% of the stay and cannot fall at the start or end
Russian Federation citizens and Russian-based host institutions are excluded, and the host must be outside the Russian Federation
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the English application form in the NAWA ICT system, upload the invitation, achievement evidence and status or employment certificates, submit before the deadline, then pass the eligibility check, the Assessment Team screening, two reviewers and the Evaluation Team before an agreement and a 90% or 60% advance payment are issued.
